Texecom Remote Power Reset

A single ESP32-C3 board inside the alarm panel housing that clears the recurring “AUX 12V output failed” fault from Home Assistant, by cutting the panel's battery and 16VAC feeds for a few seconds, then restoring them in the order Texecom specifies.

Panel
Texecom Premier Elite 64-W
Firmware

Controller
ESP32-C3 SuperMini · Tasmota
Board

Revision
Rev A · 2026-09-25
The problem

A fault that only a full power-down clears

What happens today

The panel occasionally reports AUX 12V output failed. The only way to clear it is to remove all power, battery and AC, and let the panel restart. The Texecom installation manual gives the same procedure: “Remove ALL power (AC Mains and Battery) and then reapply”.

This board does that remotely. The root cause (a tripping AUX output) is being investigated separately.

How the board does it

  • Two on-board SRD-05VDC-SL-C relays sit in the panel's battery and 16VAC feeds, wired through their normally closed contacts.
  • Home Assistant tells Tasmota to energise both relays for a few seconds, which opens the feeds.
  • The board runs from the battery side of the relay, so it stays powered while the panel is off.
  • A 74HCT4538 hardware timeout releases the relays after about 7 s, even if the ESP32 hangs.
Only reset while AC is present. The panel goes live only when AC mains returns or its kick-start button is pressed. The Home Assistant script checks AC first, so a reset during a real AC outage can't leave the panel off.
Reset sequence · drawn to scale

Battery back first, then AC

Tasmota pulses relay 1 (battery) for 3.0 s and relay 2 (AC) for 3.5 s. The battery reconnects half a second before AC, matching the manual's power-up order, and the panel goes live when AC returns. The hardware timeout sits well beyond both pulses.

System

What connects to what

Fail-safe

Every fault leaves the panel powered

The relays are energised only during a reset. The hardware timeout means relay on = GPIO high and less than about 7 s since the GPIO went high.

SituationRelay coilPanel feedsWhy
Normal reset pulse (3.0 / 3.5 s)On for the pulsecut, then restoredTimeout is longer than the pulse, so it never cuts a reset short
Firmware hangs with a GPIO stuck highOff after ~7 srestored74HCT4538 needs a new rising edge to re-trigger

Glitch on a GPIO while bootingMicroseconds onlypoweredToo short for the relay to move

Schematic · rev A

One sheet, drawn with wires

Power path across the top; channel 2 (GPIO3, AC relay K2) in the middle band and channel 1 (GPIO4, battery relay K1) below; terminals beside their relays. ERC reports 0 errors and 0 warnings, and the netlist was checked net by net against the intended circuit.

Hardware timeout (per channel)

  • GPIO → R9/R10 1k → 4538 reset (R1/R2 100k pull-down)
  • Trigger delayed 1 ms by R5/R6 10k + C7/C8 100nF
  • T = 0.7 × 1M × 10µF ≈ 7 s (TI CD74HCT4538, 5V)
  • R11/R12 100Ω in series with CEXT for power-down protection

Relay driver (per channel)

  • 4538 Q → 1k → 2N2222A, 10k base pull-down
  • 1N4007 flyback diode across the 72mA coil
  • Red LED + 1k across the coil: lit while that feed is cut
  • K1: battery (J1 → COM, NC → J2). K2: 16VAC ~A (J3 → COM, NC → J4)
PCB · rev A

Routed for an isolation-milled board

No plating, no solder mask, no silkscreen. Parts whose bodies cover their top pads carry per-pad top-side keepouts, so every connection is on a side that can be soldered. GND is poured on the bottom only; the free top copper carries an engraved legend instead, including a ring beside every pad that must also be soldered on top. DRC: 0 violations, 0 unconnected.

92 × 70 mm2 layers, 2 × M3 mounting holes
0.8 mmclearance on every net (1.0mm for 16VAC)
0.7 / 1.0 / 2.0 mmsignal / supply / battery and AC tracks
16vias, each a wire link soldered both sides
DrillHolesUsed for
0.8 mm66Resistors, disc caps, electrolytics, TO-92, DIP socket, vias
0.9 mm4LEDs
1.0 mm30SuperMini and Pololu headers, 1N4007, P6KE18A, relay coils
1.3 mm14KF301 terminals, relay contacts
1.5 mm41N5822
3.2 mm2M3 mounting holes

Assembly order

  1. ViasFit a wire through each of the 16 vias; solder both sides.
  2. Bottom SMDF1, C5, C6, R7–R12, R15, R16 (1206) on the bottom.
  3. Axial and disc partsMount 1–2mm raised and solder every pad on both sides. The 20 pads with a top track are essential and are marked on the board with an engraved ring (○ = SOLDER TOP).
  4. Everything elseTerminals, relays, socket, headers, TO-92, electrolytics, LEDs: bottom only.
  5. SuperMiniPlug in button side up with the USB-C at the right-hand board edge, following the engraved “USB →” arrow.

Milling order

  1. Alignment-pin holesOutside the board outline, so the pins are ready for the flip. With a 2.4mm fishtail at 12,000rpm: plunge at 100–150mm/min in 1mm steps with full retracts (−1, −2, −3mm), and vacuum the dust. Test the pin fit on scrap.
  2. Bottom sideHeight map first (no holes yet), then B.Cu isolation, mirrored about the pin axis: 4 passes, 15–20% overlap.
  3. Flip and re-probeOnto the alignment pins; probe a new height map on the top.
  4. Top isolationF.Cu, not mirrored, 4 passes. One pass leaves only about 0.14mm to the floating top copper (solder bridges) and copper slivers in the 0.8mm bottom gaps; 4 passes give about 0.5mm and clear the gaps. Check for slivers and shorts with a knife and a continuity meter before soldering.
  5. Legend engraveMill_Legend with the same V-bit, Z zero and height map.
  6. Drill from the topDrill file not mirrored, firm sacrificial backing, re-zero Z after each drill change; mill the 3.2mm M3 holes if needed. Z feed at 12,000rpm: 0.8mm 60–90, 1.0mm 80–120, 1.5mm 100–150, 3.2mm 120–180mm/min; single plunge to −2.0mm.
  7. Board outlineLast, no tabs: the board is held on double-sided tape (tape near the edges too). Lightly deburr the bottom pads before soldering.

Legend engrave in FlatCAM

The legend Gerber is 0.15mm lines. Use Follow geometry (Isolation Routing → Follow) so the V-bit runs once down the centre of each line instead of isolating around it.

ToolV-shape, 0.1mm tip, 30°
Cut Z−0.05 to −0.07 mm
Line widthabout 0.12–0.14 mm
Multi-depthOff (single pass)
Auto-levelUse the top height map

Apply the same offset and double-sided move as F.Cu. Every line is at least 0.35mm clear of the top copper, so a deep cut only marks floating copper. Test the depth on scrap first.

Power

Battery tap, about 13mA at idle

A Pololu S9V11E2F5 buck-boost makes 5V from the 12V lead-acid battery (solar backed), behind a 0.5A PTC, a reverse-polarity Schottky, 100µF bulk capacitance and a P6KE18A TVS. D3 stops a USB cable from back-feeding the relay rail.

State5V railFrom battery at 13.6V
Idle, WiFi connected, Tasmota Sleep 10025–35 mA11–15 mA
Reset: both relays and LEDs on for 3 s~150 mA + ESP~90 mA
Worst-case peak (WiFi TX + relays)~0.5 A~0.25 A

Bench tests · with 12–13.8V on J1, before the panel is connected

Prove it on the bench first

  1. Power-up+5V reads 4.9–5.2V; LEDs off; relays released; continuity J1+ → J2+ and J3 ~A → J4 ~A.
  2. Normal pulsePower1: K1 clicks, D6 lights, J1+ → J2+ opens for 3.0 s. Repeat with Power2 (K2, D7, 3.5 s).
  3. Hardware timeoutPulseTime1 0, then Power1: K1 releases after 5–9 s and stays off. Restore PulseTime1 30.
  4. Fail-safeUnplug the SuperMini, then pull U2: both relays stay released and the LEDs stay off.
  5. USB isolationWith J1 disconnected, plug in USB: relays, LEDs and +5V must not power up.
  6. Idle currentMeasure J1 current with WiFi connected: about 15mA or less.
Key decisions

Why it is built this way

DecisionReason
On-board relays instead of a relay moduleEach panel feed passes through 2 terminals instead of 4 terminals and 2 wires, and there is no board-to-board wiring.
74HCT4538 hardware timeoutPulseTime is software and can't release a relay if the firmware hangs with the GPIO high.
74HCT at 5V, not 74HC at 3.3VTTL inputs accept the ESP32's 3.3V, and the outputs drive the transistor bases with a full 5V.
Pololu S9V11E2F5 regulatorFixed 5V output that can't drift, and under 0.2mA idle current. The XL7015, XL4015 and MP4560 were considered and rejected.
Battery restores 0.5 s before ACMatches the Texecom power-up order: battery first, then AC.
SuperMini footprint corrected, module rotated 180°The first footprint was mirrored (it matched the bottom-view pinout drawing). Rotating the corrected module puts GPIO4/GPIO3 on the old IO pads and 5V/GND beside D3, so the routing stays as it was (DRC clean, 16 vias). USB-C now sits at the board edge; the antenna end points inward, and the V2's external-antenna option covers weak WiFi.
Per-pad top keepouts on covered partsKiCad forces plated pads onto both layers; the keepouts stop the router and the pour from making top joints that can't be soldered.
Bottom-only GND pour, engraved top legendThe top pour added little. Removing it frees the top copper for a V-bit legend (outlines, references, BAT IN / BAT OUT / AC IN / AC OUT), generated 0.35mm clear of every track and pad so it can't cut a connection.
